images.name: 01_gate-outside

images.prompt:
Lighting-only refinement of the supplied image. This image is the user's preferred material-realism reference. Preserve the exact architecture, camera angle, crop, brick bond, nuanced brick face textures and colors, clay tiles, red door and all surface detail, carvings, trees, and existing wear. Do not rebuild, beautify, denoise or repaint the materials. The goal is a real photograph with more convincing rich three-dimensional daylight transport, the sort of physically coherent illumination the user calls a ray-traced feeling, but absolutely NOT a CGI aesthetic.
Replace the somewhat flat illumination with clear mid-afternoon natural sunlight from upper camera-left, about 40 degrees high, grazing the brickwork and highlighting the relief of the tile rows and carved stone. Use one consistent sun direction. Real skylight softly fills the shadows with a slightly cooler neutral tone. Show warm indirect bounce from the sunlit pale stone steps into the recessed doorway, gradually fading deeper beneath the roof. Keep the deep recess naturally dark but with subtle reflected light on its side faces and timber joinery; no uniformly lifted shadows. Model tile overlaps and brick relief with very fine local light/shade, no artificial dark outlines or exaggerated ambient occlusion. Real soft penumbrae vary with distance from the casting object. Plausible leaf shadows from existing trees may fall subtly across an outer wall and paving, without obscuring the door. The metal knockers receive small subdued natural highlights; clay and brick remain matte and dry. Preserve realistic photographic dynamic range with detailed bright surfaces and rich shadows. Moderate perceptible increase in luminous depth and directional light, not merely a global contrast or saturation change. No glow, haze, light shafts, lens flare, wet surfaces, orange color grading or oversharpening. One full-frame photograph, no text or border.
